blocks.text: CyRSAssistant is a Windows x64 ReShade add-on. Describe a look, inspect real effect names and values, tune a preset, generate a new FX or replace an identified game pixel shader. A separate companion connects the game to your provider.

items: Install the complete ZIP beside the ReShade DLL used by the actual game executable.
Open ReShade (Home by default, or your configured shortcut), then CyRSAssistant.
Choose a provider in Connection and connect.
Ask in Chat. Review the result before saving the preset.

blocks.title: Your first session
items: Install the ZIP
Connect a provider
Describe or inspect
Review the result
Save or restore

blocks.text: Help works while disconnected and with no loaded effects. Reading it never calls a provider or changes rendering.
English is the default. Options > Language > Français switches both interface and manual immediately. The HTML manual also offers English / Français links.

Use a 64-bit Windows game and ReShade 6.8 with full add-on support. The integration targets API 20 and the ImGui 1.92.5 bridge. Native game-shader replacement supports Direct3D 11/12 pixel shaders, not every graphics API.

items: Close the game and back up an existing installation.
Find the folder containing the game’s ReShade DLL, such as dxgi.dll or d3d11.dll. Use the rendering executable’s folder, not a separate launcher.
Extract the install ZIP directly there, retaining its folders. The developer ZIP has a different layout.
Start the game, check ReShade > Add-ons / Log, then open CyRSAssistant.

blocks.text: Provider readiness is not a measure of effect quality. Check the effect status separately. Collapsing Techniques or Parameters hides rows without disabling effects.
Use Open Help window to keep the manual beside Effects or Shaders while reading. Close that window with its title-bar close control.
Use Text size to resize only the manual text; it does not change game or global ReShade settings.

items: Use Disconnect / edit before changing active settings.
Choose the provider. For an API, enter the full /chat/completions URL and the model expected by the server.
Enter a key in API key if needed; never in chat.
Click Connect. The companion starts automatically.
For CLI providers, the first normal message checks model access. A recognized login alone does not prove access or quota.

blocks.caption: Earlier development capture in French: provider selection and a recognized local Codex session. The current layout uses Connection.

blocks.text:
URL: http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/chat/completions
Model: the identifier reported by your server
API key: only if that server requires one
Remote servers require HTTPS; HTTP is accepted only on localhost. The endpoint must accept Chat Completions JSON requests and JSON responses. Local model does not install or start a model.
CLI Connect checks the local login without a model prompt. API Connect sends a small test to the selected server. Verify endpoint, login, model and quota when troubleshooting.

items: Connect and open Chat. Ordinary conversation needs no loaded effect or selected shader.
Write in Your message. Enter adds a line; Ctrl+Enter or Send submits.
Wait for progress. The response appears when finished, without streaming.
If an approval appears, inspect values/code and choose Allow this action or Deny this action.
Review the result before refining, restoring or saving.

blocks.caption: Earlier v0.4.0 capture: chat history and an FX-generation example. Data access and controls have evolved since this capture.

blocks.text: List the installed bloom FX and read their parameter names, values and ranges. Do not change anything yet.
Make colors slightly warmer while keeping current exposure. Use installed effects and report the values changed.

The assistant can page through names, values, bounds, descriptions and permitted FX/FXH sources or native inspection. Exact filenames reduce ambiguity. A hash identifies game bytecode, not its visual purpose.

New conversation clears local history and the draft, without undoing rendering. Copy conversation copies the transcript; messages also have Copy. One request runs at a time. Cancel request stops later actions; already applied changes remain active.

rows: Reads and requested edits without extra approval. One rendering operation per message.
Names and values directly readable. Each rendering edit and source/disassembly transmission needs approval.
Reads and multiple rendering operations without intermediate approval.

blocks.text: Select Options > Permission mode. The choice is saved per game. Changing mode cancels a pending request and invalidates its approvals, without restoring earlier edits.

blocks.title: Ask each time
items: Assistant proposes
Inspect values or source
Allow or deny in Chat
Apply approved action
Verify result

blocks.text: Approval belongs to one action, request and exact payload. A changed action needs another approval. Denying or cancelling interrupts the pending action. Review source-transmission summaries before approving.
Full access covers the add-on’s tools. It does not grant a terminal, arbitrary files or permissions in another AI app. External MCP writing is separately controlled by --allow-write.

items: Open Effects and Scan effects to enumerate loaded techniques and parameters.
Use Filter; expand Techniques or Parameters. Read filenames, labels, values and tooltips.
Toggle a technique or edit a value. Confirm numeric edits with Enter. Read-only values cannot be edited here.
Compare the rendering, Undo last edit when available, then Save preset only to persist the current settings.

rows: Refreshes the loaded inventory and IDs; normally clears undo.
Asks ReShade to recompile FX on the next frame.
Restores one tracked patch if values still match and the inventory remains valid.
Writes the active preset through ReShade.

blocks.text: Scan is not a compiler reload or download. After adding an FX to a configured search folder, reload effects. Performance mode or compilation errors may leave no editable values. Chat still works.

Undo has one in-memory step. Manual edits, refreshes or reloads may invalidate it. Technique order is not changed. There are no automatic historical preset backups; keep copies before substantial edits.

Ask explicitly for an addition when you want a new post-process. The assistant generates a constrained standalone FX, precompiles it, writes a new content-addressed CyRSGenerated_*.fx in a configured effect folder, reloads ReShade and checks activation.
Add an anamorphic bloom with intensity, threshold, soft knee and horizontal spread controls. Keep existing effects enabled and provide useful control ranges.

blocks.title: Generation lifecycle
items: Describe an addition
Generate and precompile
Write a new FX
Reload and initialize
Read values and verify activation

blocks.text: Up to 16 named float controls are supported. The body uses authorized screen/color sampling, time and pixel-size helpers. Unrestricted includes, declarations and loops are not accepted. Some requests exceed the generator’s capabilities.

items: Wait for the final result; compiling and initializing are intermediate states.
Read the generated filename and parameters, then inspect them in Effects or ReShade Home.
Judge the actual picture and performance. Compilation alone proves neither.
Disable last generated effect if unsuitable. The source stays on disk. Saving a preset persists activation/settings, not a visual-quality guarantee.

blocks.text: Generation reloads effects and may briefly interrupt rendering. After an error/cancellation, inspect Effects and Log before retrying. Cancel does not delete files or restore edits already applied.
FX replacement differs from adding another effect and from replacing a native game shader. Identify the exact loaded FX filename. If several bloom effects exist, ask for their names first.
Inspect loaded Bloom.fx and its controls. Replace that FX with an anamorphic version, keeping a threshold and useful intensity range. Do not add a second bloom alongside it.

items: Identify the filename and read its source/parameters when permitted.
Request an explicit replacement. Ambiguous targets need clarification. A capability question can receive an explanation before an action.
The new FX is compiled and initialized before original techniques are disabled. The original file is preserved.
Verify the new effect is active and the old techniques are off.
Restore replaced effect restores the tracked previous activation states and disables the replacement.

blocks.title: Reversible FX replacement
items: Identify original FX
Compile separate new FX
Initialize new technique
Disable original techniques
Restore tracked original if needed

blocks.text: Restoration tracks the most recent replacement in memory. Restart, reload or later changes can make it unavailable. Keep source/preset backups; this is not a permanent version history.

Shaders observes DX11/DX12 pixel shaders captured after add-on startup, identified by SHA-256 bytecode hashes. Original semantic names or HLSL are usually unavailable. Counters and bindings do not prove a shader draws the HUD, bloom or an object.

items: Refresh game shaders while the relevant scene is rendered.
Select a hash and Inspect selected shader for signatures, resources and disassembly.
Identify the intended target through actual rendering analysis, not the hash alone.
Request a replacement for that exact target. The assistant may decline an uncertain reconstruction.
After compilation and compatibility checks, the replacement is armed for subsequent game binds. Inspect the scene and restore if unsuitable.

blocks.title: Native replacement
items: Capture original bytecode
Inspect hash and contracts
Identify the target
Compile compatible HLSL
Arm subsequent binds
Restore original bindings

blocks.text: Proposed HLSL is archived under CyRSAssistant/replacements/<original-hash>/ with metadata. This is not automatic replay: restarting does not reactivate a previous replacement. Captured original bytecode remains intact.

A shared shader can affect several objects. Pixel-shader replacement cannot freely change vertex processing, resource layouts or pipeline contracts. Unsupported signatures/resources/pipelines are rejected.

In DX12, compatible graphics PSOs are rebuilt with the replacement pixel shader, preserving other stages, state and root signature. All currently required PSOs must succeed before activation. A later incompatible PSO disables the replacement with an error.

DXIL uses bundled Microsoft DXC and its validator. Register spaces, signatures and resource contracts are checked. Compilation support does not guarantee an AI can reconstruct a complex game shader faithfully.

items: Use Restore selected shader, or Restore all original shaders for the device.
Restoration takes effect on subsequent binds. Already recorded command lists can still reference the previous pipeline.
Read limitations/errors and ReShade Log. Keep the original when uncertain.

blocks.title: Why a final filter cannot always remove a HUD
items: Game scene is rendered
HUD may be composed into the same image
ReShade sees the resulting pixels
An earlier rendering stage may be needed

blocks.text: There is no automatic HUD identification or universal removal switch. A post-process cannot recover hidden scene pixels by deleting a composited HUD. CyGameCapture and CyGPUInspector are not bundled. Native replacement does not cover Vulkan, vertex stages or mesh/raytracing pipelines.

The disk catalog complements the loaded ReShade inventory. It scans configured EffectSearchPaths and TextureSearchPaths, fingerprints files and reports additions, modifications and removals. Descriptions are generated on explicit CLI request, not automatically for every effect from the overlay.

items: Use the developer package and Python 3.11+ for these commands. Specify --pipe / --runtime if discovery is ambiguous.
Run scan to update CyRSAssistant/library/catalog.json. A /** suffix on a configured path enables recursive scanning.
Resolve scan errors and duplicate FX filenames before requesting a reusable description.
Run describe with a unique filename. Source and metadata are sent to the API provider configured for this CLI request; descriptions are marked not visually verified.
Export metadata/descriptions, import them in another game with matching shader files, then rescan.

blocks.text:
python -m companion scan
python -m companion describe Tonemap.fx
python -m companion export catalogue-portable.json
python -m companion import catalogue-portable.json

Portable exports do not bundle shader sources, textures or credentials. Install required shader packs separately. A changed dependency conservatively invalidates cached analysis. Transient runtime IDs and current values are not portable shader identities.
Scanning does not download shaders or watch folders continuously. Native Scan effects enumerates loaded parameters; CLI scan inspects disk files. Keep CyRSAssistant/library during updates.

The CLI and external MCP interface can capture one current frame. Integrated chat does not automatically receive screenshots: describe what you observe after an edit. A compiled shader is not a visual comparison.
python -m companion capture capture.png

Maximum dimension is 1280 pixels. Capture performs one GPU readback and may include the ReShade overlay. It is not continuous recording and performs no HDR tone mapping. A resize during capture may require a retry.

items: Prepare the scene and request a read-only capture.
Review the image and record settings for comparison.
If using an external AI client, explicitly decide whether to send that image; its provider data policy applies.

blocks.text: The install ZIP is self-contained for the overlay. The developer ZIP adds companion/ and Python CLI/MCP modules. Run these commands from that package directory with Python 3.11+. Do not run historical watch alongside the integrated service.

python -m companion discover
python -m companion state
python -m companion scan
python -m companion ask "Make colors slightly cooler" --dry-run > plan.json
python -m companion apply plan.json
python -m companion undo
python -m companion save
python -m companion reload

ask applies changes unless --dry-run is supplied. Review a dry-run plan, then apply only to the same current session/generation/revision. Stale plans are refused. save writes the preset; undo uses the single tracked snapshot.
python -m companion --pipe "\\.\pipe\CyRSAssistant-12345" --runtime 1 state

Replace the example PID/runtime with discovery results. Global --pipe and --runtime precede the subcommand. Legacy CLI provider requests use CYRS_API_URL, CYRS_MODEL and optionally CYRS_API_KEY in the process environment; they do not reuse the overlay’s session-only key.
CLI diagnostics may expose local paths. Review them before sharing. Use the overlay connection for the standard assistant workflow; watch is a legacy manual pathway.

An external MCP client can start the developer package’s stdio server, including OpenCode or Antigravity when they support a local MCP command. These are not additional provider choices in the overlay.

python -m companion.mcp
# Opt in to writes for a trusted client:
python -m companion.mcp --allow-write

This is a generic example: each client has its own configuration format and working-directory support. Use its equivalent for the directory containing companion/. Specify --pipe for multiple games. The server pins the discovered game instead of silently switching processes.

rows: List runtimes; read names, parameters and values; capture a frame; list/inspect native shaders.

blocks.text: External MCP conversation is not copied into overlay history. MCP writing is separate from integrated permission modes. Writes still require current version tokens and valid payloads; connection does not grant arbitrary native methods or filesystem access.

Up to 16 prior messages / 24,000 characters, plus relevant request and shader/tool data.
Provider, endpoint, model, language and permissions in ReShade.ini.
Memory for the session; enter again after restart.
CyRSAssistant/replacements: proposed HLSL and metadata, without replay.
Configured shader folders / active preset, written by corresponding operations.

blocks.text: Switching providers keeps local recent history, which may accompany the next request to the newly selected provider. New conversation clears local context; it does not erase provider records or restore rendering.

blocks.title: Request data path
items: Your message and recent context
Relevant effect names and values
Authorized source/disassembly if needed
Selected provider
Validated response and tools

blocks.text: Source-reading permissions matter because code/disassembly can be transmitted. Integrated chat does not automatically see screenshots. External MCP clients independently decide what they send to models.

Provider retention, billing and account access belong to the provider. Do not type secrets in chat. Copy puts transcript contents on the clipboard; review before sharing. This manual itself is local and needs no companion or network.

rows: Confirm Windows x64, full add-on support, actual rendering executable folder, and ReShade Add-ons / Log.
Connect a provider, enter nonblank text, wait for the current request or cancel it.
First message checks model access. Verify login, model, quota and provider availability outside the game.
Check full /chat/completions URL, model, JSON support, key and server. Remote HTTP is refused.
Disconnect/reconnect. Confirm CyRSAssistantCompanion.exe is next to the add-on. Missing heartbeat is reported after ten seconds.
Reload effects; inspect compilation errors and performance mode. Chat still works.
Resolve duplicate filenames in overlapping search roots, or identify a unique loaded FX.
Read final status and ReShade Log. Correct the specific compiler error or request a simpler supported effect.
Check whether you requested addition or replacement, the exact target and technique activation.
Render the relevant scene after startup and refresh. A game update can change bytecode/hashes.
Read contract/pipeline errors. Confirm complete DXC runtime. Preserve the original.
Read current state before retrying: an action may have started. Keep the game rendering frames.
Re-extract CyRSAssistant/Documentation. Embedded Help text, images and diagrams remain available.

items: Note visible status, action, exact FX filename/hash and graphics API.
Try a limited recovery: reconnect, refresh or restore as relevant; do not resubmit edits blindly.
Collect relevant Log/compiler lines and reproduction steps only. Remove personal paths, credentials and private chat details before sharing.
Close the game before replacing binaries. Back up the add-on, companion, runtime and notices together.
Separately preserve ReShade.ini, presets, generated FX, CyRSAssistant/library and replacements.
Extract the new ZIP to the same location, merging folders. Keep Documentation and LICENCES. Do not delete the existing CyRSAssistant folder; it may contain user data.
Start and verify version, language, permissions, provider and effects. Session-only keys need re-entry.
To roll back, close the game and restore the previous matched binary/runtime/notices set. Preserve user configurations unless explicitly restoring their backups too.

blocks.text: No automatic updater is provided. Keep the matching install ZIP and corresponding developer/source ZIP. Do not mix binaries from different versions. This manual and UI translations are built for the same version.

Closing the game ends RAM-only conversations and temporary native replacements. Preset saving and keeping generated FX are different from making a native replacement persistent. This workflow does not delete backups.

rows: 32 RAM messages. Provider history: 16 prior messages / 24,000 characters. Input: 4095 UTF-8 bytes.
Automatic / Ask each time: 8 calls and one rendering operation. Full access: 16 calls and 8 rendering operations.
Up to 64 parameter/technique changes; current types and bounds are checked.
16 named float controls; constrained body without unrestricted loops/includes.
32 MiB per scanned file; JSON import up to 16 MiB; descriptions up to 20,000 characters.
DX11/DX12 pixel shaders; 4096 captured hashes / 64 MiB per device.
4096 PSO snapshots / 128 MiB, at most 4 MiB each.
Retained until device teardown; at most 64 DX11 versions or 256 DX12 PSO variants.
Single frame, maximum dimension 1280; no continuous recording or HDR tone mapping.
Protocol 1, local Windows user pipe; request up to 1 MiB, reply up to 8 MiB.

blocks.text: Session, runtime, generation and revision tokens protect against stale edits. Parameter IDs are transient indexes, not portable identities. Reload can invalidate IDs and undo. A timed-out command may already have started: read current state first.

Not implemented: shader-pack web downloading, automatic screenshot analysis in integrated chat, automatic HUD identification, Vulkan/other-stage native replacement, historical preset backups, native-replacement replay and response streaming.

rows: A render technique exposed by an FX; a file may expose several.
Effect value, possibly read-only or driven by ReShade.
Current ReShade settings file, including activation and values.
Game-rendering bytecode, distinct from a ReShade FX.
Content identity, not a visual-purpose name.
Shader-bytecode encodings handled by supported backends.
Background executable connecting the add-on to a provider.
Stdio tools interface for external clients.
Version tokens used to reject outdated edits.
